text: A Damsels' scrying glass plucked from herdstone-rubble in the Forest of Arden. Once it showed Lileath's twilight; now its visions writhe with brayhorn — yet the old runes hold against magic untrammeled.

Wrenched from the cooling skull of the last Emperor and crushed flat between Morghur's twisting horns, this dented circlet still bears Sigmar's hammer-mark beneath crusts of dried blood. Mortal men who behold it know in their marrow what comes next.
A scrying glass of the Damsels, defiled in the [[col:yellow]]Forest of Arden[[/col]] — the runes still ward those who bear it against the arcane.
Wrenched from the broken skull of [[col:yellow]]Karl Franz[[/col]] and defiled by [[col:yellow]]Morghur[[/col]] himself, the crown now bestows ruin upon all who wear it.

A flash of steel, and [[col:yellow]]Morgiana[[/col]]'s lightning never falls.
Let the baying crowds bear witness — the [[col:yellow]]Lady[[/col]]'s daughter to the dark feast.
These dunes still hide many treasures. My business is not concluded here. I shall be ready in five turns.

The Duke of [[col:yellow]]Bordeleaux[[/col]] had thought her divine, and died well for it. So had she — until I called her [[col:yellow]]Morgiana[[/col]]. She is but a girl, dressed up like a goddess by people who have never met a real one. [[col:yellow]]Khaine[[/col]] has met one. So have I. But how best to spill the blood?

The [[col:dark_r]]Asrai[[/col]] keep watchful guard, for they are surrounded by old enemies. But Drycha is ancient, and knows secrets hidden even from Orion. Lead those enemies through her hidden ways — let their ashes and the elves' alike seed a stronger [[col:yellow]]Athel Loren[[/col]]. Even as their bodies fertilize the forest floor, the enemies of the [[col:dark_r]]Asrai[[/col]] will love Drycha for it.

The relay sings. The astromantic compass burns brighter at its newly-empowered point, and a current of celestial wind rises from the heavens — bearing the Jade Dragon to whichever quarter of the Old World he wills. Where shall the Heir of the Celestial Court go next?\\n\\n[[col:cha_gold]]Ride the winds and be carried to a distant quarter of the Old World...[[/col]]

The Astromantic Relay hums with the [[col:cha_gold]]meteor winds[[/col]]. The first point of the [[col:cha_gold]]Wu Xing Compass[[/col]] is set. The other three await — but the [[col:cha_gold]]Dragon Emperor[[/col]]'s chosen has more to prove before the Old World yields its corners.

With Wulfrik the Wanderer slain, Vilitch's twin-cult unmade, and the Norscan reavers driven from the bowers of the Dreaming Wood, the twin queens stand triumphant amid the Forest of Sighs. The cluster is cleansed — Crooktail Peak silenced, the Monolith of Feytor sanctified, every camp and lodge purged of foreign blood. Now Naestra and Arahan must decide what comes next: tend the home forest in isolation, or carry the Worldroots' reach beyond Athel Loren's distant cousin?

Albion lies broken at Be'lakor's feet. The First Damned's daemonic host swells with souls torn from the island, hardened against mortal arms and emboldened to march wherever the Shadow Rifts open.

Each Legendary skull crushed beneath Be'lakor's heel feeds him. The Shadow Rifts open at his thought; mortal champions fall as wheat before the scythe. The Dark Master walks the world, and the world bleeds.
Debug-only acceleration: -50% upkeep, +500 growth, +10 horde growth, -100% construction time. Not shipped to release players.

The executioners feast upon [[col:yellow]]Morgiana[[/col]]'s body and the grail-chosen of [[col:yellow]]Carcassonne[[/col]]. [[col:yellow]]Lileath[[/col]]'s stolen strength runs in their blades, and the kingdoms still standing learn what comes for them.

With the [[col:yellow]]Fay[[/col]]'s blood, the [[col:yellow]]Brides of Khaine[[/col]] daub themselves in runes of warding — and [[col:yellow]]Bretonnia[[/col]]'s lances find only empty air where the Witch Elves had been.

The dark heart of the [[col:yellow]]Drakwald[[/col]] reshapes itself around its old master. Imperial charnel pits become birthing wallows for fresh gor-spawn, and the herds swell faster than the [[col:yellow]]Reikland[[/col]] can count its dead.
With whispered words and decapitating strokes the Jade Dragon has renewed a fractured nation — and the world's emissaries take note.

The Crone strides ashore on the misty isle — wherever Hellebron treads, the gaze of [[col:yellow]]Khaine[[/col]] follows. Frenzy sweeps the Druchii ranks; the slaves of [[col:yellow]]Albion[[/col]] fill her coffers.

[[col:yellow]]Marienburg[[/col]] burns and [[col:yellow]]Elftown[[/col]] is silent. The Witch Queen submerges herself in fresh blood — her form quickens, her sinews sing, and [[col:yellow]]Death Night[[/col]] extends another stolen year.

[[col:yellow]]Morgiana le Fay[[/col]] kneels in chains at the Witch Queen's feet. The [[col:yellow]]Lady[[/col]]'s voice is silent; the [[col:yellow]]Otherworld[[/col]] severed. Only the choosing remains.
With the Ruinous banners cast down from the northern holds, oathgold flows from the rebuilt mines and the trade-roads sing once more.
With the Ruinous banners cast down from the northern holds, oathgold flows from the rebuilt mines, trade-roads sing once more, and new gromril gates rise faster than the next host can march.

The four sacred relics returned to the White Dwarf's keeping. The Armour of Glimril Scales gleams once more, the Rune Axe sings against the gromril, the Cloak of Valaya shrouds the bearer in her favour, and the Rune Helm bears the wisdom of Zhufbar. The throng builds faster, marches further, and the White Dwarf stands immovable.

Armour of Glimril Scales gleams once more, Rune Axe of [[col:cha_gold]]Grimnir[[/col]] sings against gromril, [[col:cha_gold]]Valaya's[[/col]] Cloak shrouds the bearer in her favour, the Rune Helm of [[col:cha_gold]]Zhufbar[[/col]] restored. The White Dwarf marches further — and stands immovable.

The Legendary Grudges struck through in red — the longest grievances of the Dawi finally settled. The White Dwarf walks the world more freely now, and the blackpowder forges hum with the sustainable might of an industrialized Karaz Ankor.

The Legendary Grudges struck through in red. The grey-cloaked prospector walks the high passes more freely now, and the blackpowder forges of [[col:cha_gold]]Karaz Ankor[[/col]] hum with sustainable might.

The cracked crowns of Sylvania and Reikland rattle in Skarbrand's harness, and the Blood God leans forward upon his throne. The host moves with the swiftness of wrath, and every charge into mortal lines is the herald of a fresh skull-pile rising on the field.

Nakai's wandering host has reached its full strength. The Geomantic Web hums beneath every banner of the Defenders of the Great Plan. In battle his bulk has become a moving wall — no warmblood line can stand against the weight of him, no charge can shift his footing. The cold-blooded gaze of the Slann earns warmer welcomes from every petitioner across the world, granting Nakai's host the breathing room to consolidate before the next call.
Every Skink tribute is a verse in the [[col:yellow]]Geomantic Web's[[/col]] song. The Wanderer moves swifter for each, and strikes heavier.
Not since the [[col:yellow]]Bridge of Stars[[/col]] has Nakai's blade tasted so many defilers. [[col:yellow]]Lustria's[[/col]] spawning pools sing again with [[col:yellow]]Sotek's[[/col]] song.

The shores of Albion are lizardkind's once more. The Last Defenders' temples stand cleansed of trespassers, the geomantic wells purr beneath Saurus claws, and lizardkin scattered across the world raise their banners alongside Nakai's wandering host. The Defenders of the Great Plan grow rich under his protection, and every champion of the Old Ones strikes harder when the wandering shaman walks among them. Empire-folk, however, will long remember Wulfhart's broken expedition.
[[col:yellow]]Albion[[/col]] is lizardkind's once more — the [[col:yellow]]Defenders[[/col]] grow rich, and the Empire's hunt has ended where it began.

With the Asrai broken and their sacred waystones in ash, [[col:green]]Ariel[[/col]] emerges from the Oak of Ages. The Mage-Queen's wards are spent; her [[col:green]]Sisters of Twilight[[/col]] gather close to defend her. Throt's Packmasters sharpen their hooks — the demigoddess herself shall feed the Flesh Lab.
Word spreads of the Briarmaven's reclamation. Old enemies stir — a fateful choice will soon present itself.
[[col:yellow]]Athel Loren[[/col]] is claimed. The [[col:dark_r]]Asrai[[/col]]'s reign over the wild has ended.
The witch-puppet's deceit is undone. [[col:yellow]]Lileath's[[/col]] moon rises over the [[col:yellow]]Forest of Sighs[[/col]].

The [[col:yellow]]Worldroots[[/col]] hum beneath every Elven blade. [[col:yellow]]Daith[[/col]] hammers fresh edges into the [[col:yellow]]Talon of Dawn[[/col]] and the [[col:yellow]]Talon of Dusk[[/col]].
The Zoats of the Sherweald have pledged their undying loyalty to the Heralds of Ariel, forever grateful for their aid in cleansing the misty groves of Albion.
At the [[col:yellow]]Eternal Grove[[/col]], Hellebron's witch-elves and Drycha's branches struck the same [[col:dark_r]]Asrai[[/col]] from opposite sides — neither asking the other's intent.
The Dwarfs forget nothing. The Briarmaven offers them an [[col:dark_r]]Asrai[[/col]] reckoning.
Cyanathair's blood whispers loudest when no other voice answers. The Briarmaven walks alone.
Drycha's chant of wronged spirits has blank pages. Ogre muscle fills them.
Elven souls are the Dark Prince's hunger, and Drycha has no shortage to spend.
Drycha brought Morgiana le Fay to Mannfred without explanation. The Vampire Count's gratitude is rarely given.

The four corruptors of the Great Plan lie broken. Skryre's warpstone engines lie shattered in their burrows, the Barrow Legion's bones moulder back into the earth, the Accursed Dance is silenced beneath claw and tooth, and Aranessa's pirate-fleet rots on the southern reefs. Tehenhauin lifts his obsidian blade in salute, and the Snake-Prophet's blessing settles over Nakai's host. The wandering host marches on, hardened by victory and tempered for the long road ahead.
Throt has slain a chosen of every Ruinous Power. Archaon marches on Hell Pit — and the Castellan stands ready to claim his vengeance in blood.

<dummy>Twelve cycles he served, harbinger to other men's destinies. The thirteenth he ends — striking down each Dark Brother's chosen champion in turn, taking back the Crown of Domination, and forcing Archaon (blood of his own blood) to kneel.

<dummy>Under the light of a waxing Blood Moon, Cyanathair is reborn. A great herd harkens to his warbling cry, eager to return to the silent, unseen war that has raged eternal between the Beastmen and Wood Elves. In dark forests across the Old World, they have dealt Morghur countless defeats, but this time, he will not be denied. He will see their sacred [[col:ancillary_uncommon]]Oak[[/col]] burn, and all they hold dear turned to ash and ruin.

<dummy>Appalled by her Tormentors' lacklustre displays, Dechala vows to brew an Elixir of unmatched potency. The recipe demands a magical forest's enchanted essence and the bilious filth of Festus the Leechlord. Only then will the lowliest thrall become an instrument of exquisite torment.

<dummy>The Tallyman lifts his pen and turns his gaze northwest. Beyond the dunes of the Titan Graveyards lies a path bright with potential: Khalida's serpent-priests at Lybaras, with their cold death-cult that scorns the living rot of Nurgle, and beyond them the silver-armoured Knights of Caledor at Dramalliel's Landing, whose dragon-prince Imrik would set fire to every weeping wound in the world. Crush each in turn, march His banner over Caledor's ramparts, and the great ledger swells with new entries.

<dummy>The Carnival of Chaos has come for the bowers of Athel Loren. Epidemius marches at the head of a putrescent host, eyes fixed upon the eldest tree itself — the Oak of Ages. Slay every queen and king of the wood: Orion the Hunter, Coeddil the bound, the Wardancers of Vauls Anvil, and Durthu the ancient warden. Then crown the dying Oak with a plague-pit of His own, and let the Tallyman record every wood-elf entry beside its rotted root.

To prove his godhood among Nurgle's chosen, he must drown every isle of this fetid archipelago in His blessings, until the rivers themselves run with bilious filth and the trees weep pus. <dummy>The White Dwarf himself remembers every wrong, every betrayal, every kin-slain — the oldest pages of the Book are written in his own hand. With his panoply reclaimed and the throngs mustered behind him, the time has come to march on those legendary grudges that have hung over the Karaz Ankor since the first ancestors walked the earth.

<dummy>Forty-three names the Saga gives the wearer of the white beard — [[col:cha_gold]]Snorri Whitebeard[[/col]] returned, [[col:cha_gold]]Valaya's[[/col]] love, an Ancestor old and feared. But this one truth no Saga-verse forsakes: wherever an old grudge awaits, the [[col:cha_gold]]White Dwarf[[/col]] an appearance makes.

<dummy>When the flame of hope gutters in the northern holds, the White Dwarf walks. The Ruinous Powers gather upon Grombrindal's roads; let the next verse of the Saga be written in the snow of the high passes, that no chaos host may muster in sight of Grimnir's old paths.

<dummy>When the flame of hope gutters in the northern holds, watchfires lit brighter against the snow. But brave be thee longbeards and as all beardlings know, wherever evil stalks the [[col:cha_gold]]White Dwarf[[/col]] walks.

<dummy>Albion is bathed in Khainite blood, and still the Witch Queen's thirst is unsated. Beyond the misty isle, the Asur cling to their sun-drenched colonies — Teclis the Loremaster lectures owl-eyed acolytes among the white stones of Oeragor, Eltharion the Grim mans his lonely watchtower at Gor Gazan, and the Sea Lord Aislinn rides his black ark along the western coast hunting Slaaneshi stragglers. Slay each in turn, raise the Witch's pyres atop the loremaster and the watchman's halls, and let no echo of Aenarion's line draw breath beyond the Witch Queen's reach.

<dummy>[[col:yellow]]Morgiana[[/col]]... they call her unaging. They speak of her piercing eyes, the mist that loves her shoulders. I have not had such a morning in three hundred years. Her lifeblood mixed with that of her precious peasants will fuel my incarnation.

<dummy>They dare. The merchant princes send raiders to my shores, thinking themselves safe behind [[col:yellow]]Louen[[/col]]. He is but a boy. Soon their families will cry out as our Black Arks bombard their city walls.

<dummy>The pyres of Nagronath burn day and night, and still the Witch Queen demands more. Beyond the eastern shore lies a continent of unworthy lives — knights of Bretonnia preen in their shining castles from Lyonesse to Carcassonne, the rotting Mousillon court squats upon its throne of bone, the Skullsmasherz orcs roar across the borderlands, and the dwarfs of Karak Ziflin hammer at their forges in the Blackstone Tower. Drag every soul to Khaine's altars: fifteen thousand captives shall scream in the Witch Queen's name, and the lords of the south shall be the centerpiece of the rite.

<dummy>The Brides of Khaine kneel as her wolf-prows beach. [[col:yellow]]Crone Hellebron[[/col]], Blood Queen of Har Ganeth, second only to Morathi in their god's sight — and where she treads, [[col:yellow]]Khaine[[/col]]'s gaze follows.

<dummy>The Witch Queen rises from her bloodied sanctum at Nagronath as the screams of a thousand sacrifices ride the western wind. Beyond her cold shore lies an island of false thrones — the Jade Emperor whispers Cathayan prayers from Llenog's spire, the Shadow King creeps through Trogland's stone circles loosing his cursed arrows, an Empire huntsman struts across Neuland with his bow raised in vain, and lizard-men of the lost city Konquata bask in the heat of dying suns. Cleanse them all in Khaine's name, draw every menhir and barrow-mound under the Witch Queen's blade, and Albion shall be the first kingdom of an eternal slaughter.

<dummy>The Architect of Fate is no nomad — his domain is the Crystal Labyrinth itself, that shifting realm of mirrors and prophecy at the world's south-western edge. Frozen Moon, Eternity Stair, the Heavenward Halls and the Ninth Library; the Obsidian Council, the Crystal Labyrinth itself, and every other monolith and observatory in the chaos wastes — all must answer to the Lord of Change. Cleanse the encroaching rot of Septic Claw and claim the realm of Tzeentch in full.

<dummy>The Architect of Fate turns his gaze northward, away from the dune-tombs and toward the upstart prophets of mankind. Volkmar the Grim chants Sigmar's revelations from Nachtdorf, charting fates by hammer-strokes and faith. Elspeth von Draken bends the Gunnery School of Nuln to her will, casting futures in molten lead. Both wizard-priests would write tomorrow without the Architect's leave. Silence them, claim their books and crucibles, and the Old World's prophecies shall flow only from Tzeentch's beak.

<dummy>The Lord of Change drinks deep from the well of bygone ages. In the dunes south of Frozen Moon, the great dynasties of Nehekhara keep secrets older than the gods themselves — Khalida's serpent-mummies guard whispered prayers from the dawn of the Mortuary Cult, the dust-dry priests of Khemri stand watch over the Great Necropolis, and Arkhan the Black has bound Nagash's stolen lore to his cold tongue. Tear those secrets from their decaying lips, claim the Black Pyramid for Tzeentch, and the Lord of Change's library swells with truths the Old World has long forgotten.

<dummy>“You look down on us and think we are little better than barbarians, but you should be glad we are, for without us here, the daemons and devil worshippers would be dining on the flesh of your children in your burning homes. But for the courage that flows in our veins would your lands be theirs. Look down on us? You should be on your knees, thanking us every day!”

<dummy>“You look down on us and think we are little better than barbarians, but you should be glad we are, for without us here, the enemies of the north would be dining on the flesh of your children. But for the courage that flows in our veins would your lands be theirs. Look down on us? You should be on your knees, thanking us every day!”

<dummy>The Pit awakens. Throt's warp-fused horde erupts from Hell Pit's nine wounds, and around it gather Khorne's daemons and the orcs of the eastern crags — Skarbrand bellowing for blood at the gates, the Bloody Queen at the head of her gore-soaked riders, Azhag the Slaughterer raiding in their wake. The boyars must rally their pulks and storm the three holds of the Pit, that no warp-thing shall raze another stanitsa within the Tzarina's reach.

<dummy>Kislev has many enemies. While we fight among ourselves they take advantage. While we preach sermons they raid our borders. But they have underestimated us. For we are [[col:yellow]]Kislev[[/col]]. And we bow to no one!

<dummy>The Bear-Tzar's cult kindles its winter fires, and Skarbrand grins as the smoke reaches Khorne's nostrils. Cross the frozen oblast in a wave of cloven steel — silence Ursun's priests at Erengrad, drag the Tzarina from her glass throne in Kislev, and let Praag burn a second time. By the time the Bear-Tzar's blood freezes on his axe, the road south shall be open and trembling.

<dummy>[[col:dark_r]]BEAR-TZAR[[/col]]. Glass throne — easy to crack. [[col:dark_r]]Tzarina[[/col]], witch-Tsar, priest of Ursun: SKULLS for the pile. [[col:dark_r]]Praag[[/col]] burns FIRST. Skarbrand has come for the Bear.

<dummy>The mountain-clad children of Grungni cower behind their rune-locked gates, mistaking their stone for shelter. Skarbrand drinks deeply from the Worlds Edge — Karaz-a-Karak, Karak Kadrin, Zhufbar. Their forges shall be quenched in dwarf-blood, their throngs broken upon black axe-edges, their oaths swallowed by the wind. Where ancestor-runes once glowed, only ash and the laughter of the Blood God shall remain.
<dummy>[[col:dark_r]]DAWI[[/col]]. Stone walls. Oath-locked gates. STONE CRACKS. The [[col:dark_r]]Slayer-King[[/col]] falls FIRST. Skarbrand REMEMBERS [[col:dark_r]]Karak Angkul[[/col]].

<dummy>The road south curves between the mausoleums of dead empires and the marble halls of one still pretending to live. Sylvania's vampire prince calls the dead from rotting Drakenhof; Reikland's Emperor counts coppers atop the South Bank. Skarbrand cares for neither title nor pact — only the blood, only the skulls. Drag both kingdoms to ruin, mount both crowns on the same crooked pike, and let the Skull Throne grow a hand's breadth higher.
<dummy>TWO crowns. [[col:dark_r]]Vampire-prince[[/col]]. [[col:dark_r]]Soft Emperor[[/col]]. One plays at death, one at life — both BLEED. The Throne wants both.

<dummy>The Ice Queen leads a fractured nation, under threat from forces both without and within. [[col:yellow]]Kostaltyn[[/col]], the de facto leader of the Great Orthodoxy, instigates rebellion from his stronghold on the west coast. His sermons were well-received by the [[col:yellow]]Ropsmenn Clan[[/col]], who have risen out of the ghettos of [[col:yellow]]Praag[[/col]] to take control of the city.

<dummy>Karl Franz watches over the Empire from his marble throne, and beneath his gaze the lands of men rest easy. Topple him. Wrench the crown from his lifeless skull, wear it broken and defiled upon your horned brow, and let every mortal yet drawing breath tremble and despair before you.

<dummy>Karl Franz sits the marble throne untroubled — the omens have not yet reached him. But Morghur remembers when the [[col:yellow]]Drakwald[[/col]] was his. The god-Emperor wears a crown that calls to horned brows.

<dummy>On the storm-wracked island of Albion, an outpost of the Old Ones' children stands besieged. The Last Defenders — Nakai's lizardkin, sworn to guard the geomantic wells of the cold isle — bleed beneath three hammers: Wulfhart's Hunt-Marshals stalking the moors for trophies, Be'lakor's daemon shadows boiling out of every standing stone, and Hellebron of Har Ganeth descending to bathe in lizard blood. Whether to avenge fallen kin or rescue those still drawing breath, Nakai turns his wandering host north. Break the three besiegers, secure the twelve sacred regions of Albion, and the Old Ones' island shall be lizardkind's once more.

<dummy>In storm-wracked [[col:yellow]]Albion[[/col]], the [[col:yellow]]Last Defenders[[/col]] beat the temple-drums for help. Three thousand miles south, in the deep jungle, the [[col:yellow]]Wanderer[[/col]] remembers [[col:yellow]]Tlanxla[[/col]] burning. This time, he is closer.

<dummy>From the spawning pools of southern Lustria, the Snake-Prophet Tehenhauin lifts his obsidian dagger and calls Nakai's wandering host to a great purification. Ikit Claw's warpstone engines poison the deep places of the world; Aranessa Saltspire's pirates drag the Tilean coasts into ruin; Heinrich Kemmler awakens the barrow-dead to march beneath the moon; and the Masque of Slaanesh whirls her Accursed Dance through every court she can corrupt. Each is a wound on the Great Plan, each must be cauterised. Where the wandering host treads, no corruptor's banner shall remain standing.

<dummy>Older Skinks remember the [[col:yellow]]Rise of Sotek[[/col]] — how the [[col:yellow]]Wanderer[[/col]] came when [[col:yellow]]Tehenhauin's[[/col]] dagger first met Pestilens. The Snake-Prophet lifts the obsidian again, and the [[col:yellow]]Cult of Sotek[[/col]] hopes.

<dummy>Nakai's host wanders without rest, gifting every settlement his Saurus seize to the Defenders of the Great Plan. Slay five Legendary Lords of the Old Ones' enemies, raise fifteen Defender banners across the world, and bring low Ku'gath the Plaguefather and Wurrzag, Da Great Green Prophet — only then will the Geomantic Web reveal its next call.

<dummy>At the bonfires of [[col:yellow]]Itza[[/col]], Skink priests tell the little ones of the jungle-spirit [[col:yellow]]Nakai[[/col]], who appears when all seems lost. The older priests shrug. But in their hearts they hope.

<dummy>Seafang rips free of the Realm of Chaos in a storm of howling aethyr and comes crashing down upon the sweltering shores of [[col:yellow]]Skeggi[[/col]]. The Norscan settlers watch in awe as Wulfrik strides ashore, his tribesmen pounding down the gangplank behind him. Beyond the settlement’s crude walls, the Lustrian jungle looms – concealing temple-cities laden with golden treasures and cold-blooded beasts eager to meet the Wanderer’s blade.

<dummy>Cursed to wander the world without end, Wulfrik is driven to seek out great warriors and challenge them to single combat. Mortal champions, daemonic princes, revenant kings – he will cut them down one-by-one, or fall forgotten on some distant shore. Either way, the gods will have their due.

<dummy>The twin-souled queens walk the ancient bowers of the Forest of Sighs. Northward, [[col:dark_r]]Wulfrik[[/col]] profanes the sacred groves with Norscan steel; westward, [[col:dark_r]]Vilitch the Curseling[[/col]] and his Puppets of Misrule mock the twin-born to Tzeentch's purpose. Cleanse the home cluster and slay both archfoes.

<dummy>At the [[col:yellow]]Temple of Lileath[[/col]] in the [[col:yellow]]Forest of Sighs[[/col]], the Maiden of the Moon shows her priestesses the same dream every dawn: a witch-laughing curseling, and a wood that does not yet dream. [[col:yellow]]Naestra[[/col]] and [[col:yellow]]Arahan[[/col]] have seen it too.

<dummy>The Oak of Ages stands at the heart of the Worldroots, ancient beyond measure and irreplaceable. The Sisters' twin-souled prophecy turns dark — axes, gnaw-pits, beast-horns, and grave-cairns gather around the eldest tree. The dwarfs of Karak Norn fell trees by the thousand to feed their forges. Lord Skrolk's pestilens-monks chew the World-Roots from below. Khazrak's beastmen dance bloody rites in the surrounding glades. Vlad von Carstein hungers for the sap of the eldest tree to fuel his necromancy. Slay each in turn, and ensure every glade and forest of Athel Loren — from Kings Glade to Tal Amere, from Karak Norn to Blood Keep — flies under friendly banners before the Oak is brought low.
Perform the Rite of Rebirth at the [[col:yellow]]Oak of Ages[[/col]].

<dummy>With the home heartwood safe, the Sisters may turn outward. A great Zoat lumbers from the Worldroots to the Oak of Ages and kneels: the [[col:green]]Sherweald[[/col]] — Athel Loren's distant cousin amid the misty isles of Albion — sickens, and the ancient guardian asks aid. Druchii cultists, a drifting Shadow Legion castle, and cold-blooded Lustrians have made playground of the far cousin's groves. Cleanse them, and the Sherweald shall bloom anew.

<dummy>A great Zoat of the [[col:yellow]]Sherweald[[/col]] walks into the [[col:yellow]]Eyrie of Twilight[[/col]] and kneels — the misty groves sicken, and [[col:yellow]]Hoeth's[[/col]] altar in the [[col:yellow]]Forest of Fagmar[[/col]] stands cold. [[col:yellow]]Naestra[[/col]] saddles [[col:yellow]]Gwindalor[[/col]]; [[col:yellow]]Arahan[[/col]] mounts [[col:yellow]]Ceithin-Har[[/col]].

<dummy>The Worldroots stretch across the world, but their heart has grown thin. The Mage-Queen calls: reclaim the magical forests, carry the rite of rebirth to each, and defend the Oak of Ages itself. Only then is the Sisters' twin-souled prophecy fulfilled.

<dummy>In a dream the [[col:yellow]]Mage Queen[[/col]] speaks: the [[col:yellow]]Worldroots[[/col]] grow thin, and the [[col:yellow]]Oak of Ages[[/col]] hungers. [[col:yellow]]Naestra[[/col]] and [[col:yellow]]Arahan[[/col]] ride out at the same hour — sunrise and sunset bleeding into one.

<dummy>The wary-wise of the [[col:dark_r]]Lords of Decay[[/col]] whisper-doubt Throt-Master's worth — yes-yes, they sabotage his slabs, they mock his brood. Let them see-see now: thirteen bells, ten thousand chittering sons, the man-things dragged home in chains.

<dummy>Yes-yes, the [[col:green]]Mage-Queen[[/col]] hides — long-long aeons behind her wood-witch wards, untouchable, unkillable. Snap the wards, force her into the open, and for the first time in ages [[col:dark_r]]Clan Moulder[[/col]] shall feast on a goddess's blood.

<dummy>The [[col:dark_r]]Flesh Lab[[/col]] roars hungry and must be fed. Three chosen of the Ruinous Powers infest the lower circles — drag every champion back to the lab in pieces. Beyond the iron-and-bone gates an older debt waits: [[col:dark_r]]Sarthorael the Ever-Watcher[[/col]], Throt's arch-rival of long centuries, holds his thousand-eyed vigil over the pit so that no rat may climb out and no tribute may flow in.

<dummy>The shifting sands of Nehekhara hide many long lost tombs filled with powerful magical artefacts that Mannfred desires. They also hide many foes who would see him undone. They will find only death and an unlife of eternal servitude in these dunes.

<dummy>The time has come to return to Sylvania and reclaim the von Carstein's ancestral citadel: Castle Drakenhof. In his private chambers in the uppermost tower, Mannfred can continue to study the Books of Nagash he has found thus far. But first, Vlad and Isabella must be convinced to recognise his supremacy, or else be staked through the heart and left out for dawn's light to take them.
<dummy>“This world is mine. It did not belong to Vlad and it does not belong to Nagash or the Dark Gods. It was promised to me in my cradle, and I will have what I am owed.”
<dummy>Mannfred has bided his time since his defeat at Hel Fenn. Now, he has returned to launch an unholy assault upon the Empire. The reign of the Midnight Aristocracy is nigh...

<dummy>As the first true Vampire Count, Vlad has designs not only to create a realm of the dead, but also to secure dominion over the living. Together with his wife, Isabella, he wages war against the Empire, for he truly believes he has a legitimate claim to the throne.

<dummy>Vlad's ambitions turn eastward, to the lands of the Dwarfs. Beneath their bastions of stone, an untouched realm of ancient treasure vaults and burial tombs lies concealed. These chambers are sealed with potent runic wards, safeguarding their honoured dead and the glittering treasure hoards within. For the von Carsteins, such spoils are too tempting to ignore.

<dummy>[[col:yellow]]Kattarin the Bloody[[/col]] once ruled Kislev as its tzarina before she was ousted from the throne and staked through the heart by her great-great-grandson, Tsaravich Pavel. Her corpse, frozen in a block of ice, is still on display at [[col:yellow]]Bokha Palace[[/col]], much to the chagrin of the Midnight Aristocracy. Upon learning of this tale, Isabella was outraged. She has vowed to punish the Kislevites for their temerity, though others suspect she merely wishes to see the [[col:yellow]]Ice Queen[[/col]] dead, for her cold beauty is rumoured to rival Isabella's own...

<dummy>Bound to the [[col:yellow]]Glade of Woe[[/col]] since before the [[col:dark_r]]Asrai[[/col]] dared step foot in the green, Drycha has chanted two thousand years' worth of wronged spirits' names. Now men of the Old World hack and burn what has stood since the Forgotten Season — and in his [[col:yellow]]Wildwood[[/col]] prison [[col:yellow]]Coeddil[[/col]] still slumbers.

<dummy>While the [[col:dark_r]]Asrai[[/col]] cower behind Athel Loren's borders, the Briarmaven walks the forests they abandoned, twisting each in her image. Naieth the Prophetess cannot see Drycha's path — it is drenched in blood.

<dummy>The [[col:dark_r]]Asrai[[/col]] strangle the [[col:yellow]]Oak of Ages[[/col]] with their meddling. They call it guardianship; Drycha calls it the long murder. The Briarmaven will pull every Asrai root from her forest, no matter what daemon she must bargain with to do it.

<dummy>Wulfrik bears an old grudge against Alberic of Bordeleaux, the bold knight whose lance has cost the Seafang's crew dearly. The prow shall not turn from the Lyonesse coast until Bordeleaux is sundered and Alberic feeds the waves.

<dummy>A hooded crone steps from the moonlit mists of Albion — Quai Yin, the Moon Empress and Yuan Bo's mother, hidden in mortal guise. The End Times approach; this fractured island must be made whole before the celestial mandate may extend further. The Druchii of Har Ganeth perch on its eastern bluffs, scaled Lustrians prowl its mossy hollows, and the Drifting Castle of Be'lakor casts a baleful shadow upon its northern shore. Cleanse them all — Albion shall be the first throne of a reunited Celestial Order.

<dummy>Through the moonlit mists of [[col:cha_gold]]Albion[[/col]] the [[col:cha_gold]]Jade Dragon[[/col]] walks, the jade eyes of his armour aglow with his mother's distant watching.
